candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a hard, yellowish-white, well-delineated calcification protruding through the right palatine tonsil with radiographic ovoid calcification in the tonsillar region. This is consistent with a tonsillolith (tonsillar calculus), not sialolithiasis. While both involve calcification in the head and neck, sialolithiasis involves salivary gland ductal obstruction (typically submandibular, parotid, or sublingual), which does not match the tonsillar location, appearance, or presentation described.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Sialolithiasis refers to calculi within salivary glands/ducts; tonsillolith refers to calcification within tonsillar crypts — distinct anatomical structures and pathological entities

case_quality_flags: Betel-nut chewing and tobacco use noted but not relevant to tonsillolith diagnosis; may have been included as distractors or to raise malignancy concern, which was appropriately excluded by nasopharyngoscopy findings.
